summary: `color_hex` is normalized and stored without its `#` prefix end-to-end, but `additional_color_hexes` retains a literal `#` on every comma-joined value, in both the generator (catalog-tool) and the Android-side digest/entity — an avoidable format inconsistency that is currently harmless only because `normalizeHex()` is applied at every consumption site.
claim: No functional break exists today because `OpenSpoolCodec`/`validateRecord`'s `normalizeHex()` strips `#` defensively wherever these values are actually used, but any future code that displays, compares, or hashes `additionalColorHexes` without going through `normalizeHex()` would silently produce a `#`-prefixed value inconsistent with the bare `colorHex` convention.

evidence.source: catalog-tool/CatalogTool.kt's `colors()` returns `colors.map { "#${normalizeHex(it)}" }`; the TSV writer emits the first color (`color_hex` column) and remaining colors (`additional_color_hexes` column, `colors.drop(1).joinToString(",")`) both still carrying `#`. `contentDigest()` normalizes only `index==7` (color_hex) by stripping `#`, never doing so for `additional_color_hexes` (index 17). On the Android side, `Databases.kt`'s `ensureCatalog()` strips `#` when building `CatalogEntry.colorHex` (`f[7].removePrefix("#")`) but does not strip it for `additionalColorHexes` (`f[17]` stored as-is), and `catalogDigest()` mirrors this asymmetry exactly (matching, so digests still agree between generator and app).

suggested_remediation: Normalize `additional_color_hexes` the same way as `color_hex` (store/hash without `#`) at the point of catalog generation, keeping the two fields' on-disk conventions consistent.
suggested_validation: Generate a catalog entry with two colors, confirm `additionalColorHexes` is stored without `#` prefixes and that `catalogDigest()`/`contentDigest()` remain in agreement between catalog-tool and the Android app after the change.
